# MDL002 · `invalid-suppression`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

A suppression comment is malformed, names an unknown rule, or targets MDL1xx.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | suppressions |
| Default severity | warning |
| Fix | — |
| Flags | unsuppressible |

## Why

Directives are `# mydumper-lint: disable-next-line=ID,…` and `# mydumper-lint: disable-file=ID,…`, with rule IDs or names. A directive without rules, with an unknown rule or with another verb does nothing. MDL1xx diagnostics mean mydumper ignores the whole file: they cannot be suppressed by comments, only by the configuration or `--ignore`. A directive must not contain `[`, which would change how mydumper's pre-processor reads the following lines.

## Example

❌ Before:

```ini
[mydumper]
# mydumper-lint: disable-line=MDL402
# mydumper-lint: disable-file=
# mydumper-lint: disable-file=MDL402 [x]
threads=4
```

```text
2:1-2:37 warning MDL002[invalid-suppression] unknown suppression "disable-line=MDL402": use `disable-next-line=ID,…` or `disable-file=ID,…`
3:1-3:31 warning MDL002[invalid-suppression] the suppression names no rule: list rule IDs or names after `=`
4:1-4:41 warning MDL002[invalid-suppression] a suppression comment must not contain `[`: mydumper's pre-processor would not reset its state after it
```

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL002: warning   # or error, info, off
```

Its diagnostics mean mydumper ignores the whole file: they cannot be suppressed by comments, only by the configuration or `--ignore`.
